name: @projexlight/connector-salesforce
summary: Bidirectional Salesforce connector for ProjexCloud: OAuth install + bind ProjexCloud entities (lead, contact, account, opportunity) to their SF counterparts, run scheduled syncs in both directions, ingest SF Platform Events via webhook. Foundation for any revops blueprint that wants 'system of record' parity between ProjexCloud + the tenant's Salesforce org.

events.name: connector-salesforce.install.created.v1
events.description: Tenant completed SF OAuth + the connector recorded their org.

events.name: connector-salesforce.binding.created.v1
events.description: Entity binding registered (ProjexCloud type ↔ SF object + sync direction).

events.name: connector-salesforce.sync.failed.v1
events.description: Sync run failed; carries error class + which entity.

events.name: connector-salesforce.webhook.received.v1
events.description: Inbound SF Platform Event committed for projection.

models.description: Cached SF Account row (read-through cache; full row is in SF).

hooks.name: installConnector
hooks.description: Begin OAuth flow; on callback, store refresh token in sdk-secrets + record the SF org.

hooks.name: registerBinding
hooks.description: Wire a ProjexCloud entity type to its SF counterpart + sync direction (push / pull / merge).

hooks.name: runSyncNow
hooks.description: Force a sync run for one binding; useful after the customer fixes a permission gap.

hooks.name: handleWebhook
hooks.description: Verify + ingest a SF Platform Event payload (called from the webhook receiver route).

hooks.name: startScheduler
hooks.description: Background worker that drives scheduled syncs + token refresh.

scenarios.title: Tenant admin clicks 'Connect Salesforce' → OAuth + install
scenarios.when_to_use: First-time setup. The admin signs in via SF; we exchange the auth-code for a refresh token + store it in sdk-secrets.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Install row written; refresh token vault-stored. Emits .install.created.v1. Connector page shows green health dot.

scenarios.title: Push ProjexCloud lead-scores into SF Lead records
scenarios.when_to_use: RevOps workflow: lead-scoring computed in ProjexCloud pushes back to SF Lead.Lead_Score__c every 15 min.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Binding row + scheduler tick. Sync runs every 15 min push fresh scores; conflicts (e.g. SF row deleted) land in sync_run with the error class.

scenarios.title: After fixing a permission gap, force-resync now
scenarios.when_to_use: SF admin granted the API user write access to a custom field; we want the next sync to happen immediately not at the next scheduled tick.
scenarios.example_code:
import { runSyncNow } from '@projexlight/connector-salesforce';
const { sync_run_id } = await runSyncNow({ binding_id });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Sync run executes; result emitted via .sync.completed.v1 or .sync.failed.v1.

scenarios.title: SF Platform Event 'OpportunityClosedWon' → ProjexCloud action
scenarios.when_to_use: Inbound webhook for real-time signals. SF fires a Platform Event when Opp closes; we ingest + emit .webhook.received.v1 so downstream SDKs (sdk-billing, sdk-notification) react instantly.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Payload signature verified; event committed + emitted. Downstream consumers fan out within seconds (no polling latency).

scenarios.title: Reactive: re-validate after secrets rotation
scenarios.when_to_use: secrets.secret.rotated.v1 fires for the SF refresh-token secret; the connector re-tests connectivity before relying on it.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Each install probed; failures disable the install + page ops.

compliance_posture.notes: OAuth refresh token always vault-wrapped (never logged or persisted in plain). EU tenants pin to SF EU instances; sync direction respects the customer's Shield-PII field-level encryption settings. Webhook signature verification mandatory; replay-window enforced to defeat replay attacks.
